_readme: Feasibility rubric for local ratings. STRUCTURE (six dimensions; High / Medium / Low; plus a limited-evidence / no-evidence state, LE/NE) follows IPCC AR6 WGII Cross-Chapter Box FEASIB (Ch. 18, Fig. FEASIB.2), checked against the figure caption 2026-09-26. The one-line LEVEL DESCRIPTIONS are adapted from the per-option justifications in IPCC AR6 WGII Ch. 3 Table SM3.3 (rows named in `fromRows`); neither source gives formal level definitions, so the wording is reasoned_extrapolation, not verbatim IPCC text. The six dimensions follow Singh et al. (2020); Ch. 3 pairs them as given in `ar6Pair`.

levels.High: Low costs or high economic returns relative to cost; no significant economic barrier.
levels.Medium: Economically possible but with large or high costs that need dedicated public or private investment.
levels.Low: High costs (e.g. relocation, new infrastructure) make it economically hard to implement.

levels.High: Technology is mature and in widespread use.
levels.Medium: Technologically ready but at adaptation-planning or early-implementation stage, or needs high technical capacity.
levels.Low: Early planning stage with little implementation; technical readiness not demonstrated.

levels.High: High political acceptability; supporting institutions and regulatory framework already in place.
levels.Medium: Mixed regulation and governance; institutions not designed for it, but no major transformation needed.
levels.Low: Rigid institutions or legal barriers; not implemented in existing governance; would need transformational change.

levels.High: High social acceptability; supports equity, participation and co-management; social co-benefits.
levels.Medium: Generally accepted, but can disbenefit some groups or cause conflict if not well designed.
levels.Low: Likely conflicts between communities or groups; risks loss of livelihood, identity or increased vulnerability.

levels.High: Supports ecosystem services and biodiversity; provides ecological resilience; no known trade-offs.
levels.Medium: Transforms natural habitats while aiming to maintain ecosystem services, or has mixed effects.
levels.Low: Irreversible environmental change or added pressure on the environment.

levels.High: Physically feasible at the needed scale; the setting already supports it.
levels.Medium: Possible but scope or scalability is limited (e.g. by materials, footprint or habitat type).
levels.Low: Not physically feasible in many settings (e.g. constrained by urbanised coastline or physical limits).

evidenceState.label: Limited / no evidence (LE/NE)
evidenceState.description: Someone looked, and the evidence to rate this dimension is limited or absent. Distinct from 'Not assessed' (nobody has looked yet). IPCC AR6 CCB FEASIB uses this state alongside high / medium / low.
